mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thus driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are not positive when UNRATE is below 5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in federal funds rate above 5% tightens monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs rise.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) increases and unemployment (UNRATE) decreases, it indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not increase when both PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, slowing industrial production (INDPRO) indicates reduced corporate output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive when INDPRO growth is below 2% YoY in a late-cycle expansion, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not increase when HOUST rises, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in CPIAUCSL above 210 indicates inflationary pressures, potentially leading to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive when CPIAUCSL exceeds 210, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows and retail sales (RSAFS) also increase, it signals strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not increase when both GDPC1 and RSAFS grow, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDP (GDPC1) during a recession indicates reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive during a recession when GDPC1 declines, this hypothesis fails.
